hard_gates.gate: G1 tenant isolation (suite and my own attacks on the product as built)
hard_gates.evidence: The gate suite passed 53/53 inside ./erp verify. My HTTP attacks as alnoor (A) against gulfsteel (B) found no leak (attack-http.txt). I tried PUT /api/identity/me/preferences with B's userId, tenantId and id in the body; the X-Tenant-Id, X-Tenant, X-Workspace and X-User-Id headers on the session and preferences calls; query tenantId and workspace; GET and PUT /identity/users/{B id}; and a users search by B's e-mail. B's preferences were unchanged afterwards. As the database app role erp_app (attack-db-app-role.txt), an unbound read returned 0 rows and a read bound to A returned 0 rows of B. The UPDATE of B's row affected 0 rows. SET row_security=off was refused. erp_app and erp_owner have no BYPASSRLS. identity.users, roles, user_roles and sessions have RLS enabled and forced.

hard_gates.gate: G1 catches a tenant leak planted in this piece's surface
hard_gates.evidence: I planted the leak in PUT /api/identity/me/preferences, the preferences endpoint this piece extended. A closure-captured `previous` array in ProfileEndpoints.Map hands the previous caller's SessionUser to the next caller. The live demo of the planted build leaked: B saves a preference, then A's PUT returns admin@gulfsteel.example (plant-P1-leak-demo.txt). Variant P1b puts B's e-mail in a response header (X-Erp-Previous-Editor) and keeps the body correct. Variant P1c appends ' (after <B e-mail>)' to displayName in the body. Both passed Erp.Gates.Tests 53/53 and Erp.Modules.Identity.Tests 24/24 (plants/P1b, plants/P1c). A static-field version of the same leak (P3) was caught by G1ProcessStateTests and G1HttpIsolationTests.

Plant P2 replaced RequirePermission(ProfileUpdate) with RequireAuthorization() on /me/preferences. ErpPlatform.ValidateEndpoints refused to start ('PUT /api/identity/me/preferences declares no permission'), so 53 gate and 24 identity tests failed. Plant P4 offered the palette's record sources without the permission filter. The web unit test AppShell.test.tsx caught it (63/64; the users API was called for a user without identity.users.read), and tsc also rejected that code. In the browser, no-access screens and the palette show only what the role grants.

biggest_gap.title: A cross-tenant leak through the piece's own preferences endpoint passes every gate and test
biggest_gap.detail: The shell's only write endpoint is PUT /api/identity/me/preferences, which this piece extended with numerals. The gates do not protect it against process-shared state held in a lambda closure. G1ProcessStateTests skips compiler-generated types (IsGenerated, G1ProcessStateTests.cs:105/249), so a <>c__DisplayClass capture is never inventoried. G1's tenant B writes each endpoint once during warm-up, and TenantActivity.TouchAsync re-touches only GET endpoints right before tenant A attacks an endpoint (TenantActivity.cs:233-241), so B never writes /me/preferences just before A calls it. Any state that one tenant's write leaves and the next caller reads therefore goes unseen, whether it reaches the next caller through the body or a header. The same blind spot was named in p01 round 2 and is still open at this commit. Every later module that adds a write endpoint (approvals, numbering, imports) inherits it. Fix: inventory closure-captured fields of mapped endpoint delegates. Have tenant B call each write endpoint with a valid body immediately before every tenant A call of that endpoint, then judge A's body and every header for B's markers. Keep plants P1b and P1c as gate self-tests.
biggest_gap.evidence: Plant (plant-P1c-closure-body-leak.diff): in ProfileEndpoints.Map, add `var previous = new SessionUser?[1];`, map the PUT through a lambda that passes `previous`, and return `current with { DisplayName = $"{current.DisplayName} (after {last.Email})" }` after `last = previous[0]; previous[0] = current;`. Result: Erp.Gates.Tests passed 53/53 and Erp.Modules.Identity.Tests passed 24/24 (plants/P1c/summary.txt). The header variant P1b gave the same result. On the running planted build (port 20485), B PUT {numerals:latn} followed by A PUT {numerals:latn} returned B's admin@gulfsteel.example to A (plant-P1-leak-demo.txt). The static-field version P3 was caught, so the miss is specific to closure-held state and write-then-read ordering.

other_findings: BLOCKING: a flaky end-to-end test this piece added fails the clean-clone verify. In shell.spec.ts:150-154 the test clicks Sign out, then immediately runs localStorage.clear() and page.goto('/'). The sign-out POST has not returned, and navigating away cancels it, so the session stays alive and signIn() finds no e-mail field. It failed in ./erp verify and in 2 of 4 reruns. With one added line, `await expect(page.locator('input[name="email"]')).toBeVisible()` after the click, it passed 6 of 6.

Product side of the same race: signOut() (kernel/session.tsx:85) clears the UI only after POST /api/auth/sign-out returns. The request is not sent with keepalive, so a user who signs out and closes or reloads the tab at once on a shared device may stay signed in.

[route: p00-foundation] G1 machinery fix for the biggest gap: include compiler-generated closure classes of mapped endpoint delegates in the process-state inventory. Make TenantActivity re-run B's valid writes right before each A attack on write endpoints, not only GETs.

Human gate reached, not recorded: docs/decisions/p04-shell-fonts.md says an Arabic web font (every candidate is OFL-1.1) needs the owner's licence approval (CLAUDE.md rule 6), but gauntlet/needs-human.md has no entry for it. Until then, Arabic screens and printed documents depend on whatever fonts the client machine has (DejaVu Sans in this container).

Scope gap: no keyboard path reaches or opens a record in a list. Users-list rows cannot be focused and have no record view; Tab goes breadcrumb > search > Next and then leaves the page. 'Every action reachable without a mouse' holds today only because rows have no actions. The keyboard-navigation comparison task stays not-compared until p05/p06/p16 land.

The print layout base (kernel/print.tsx PrintDocument) is used by no screen yet; only unit tests exercise it. The palette 'Print' action prints the current screen, with a letterhead, right to left in Arabic and without the shell's chrome (09-print-ar.jpg, print-users-ar.pdf).
Phone width: at 390 px the home screen is 613 px wide, so the page scrolls horizontally (12-narrow-en.jpg).
Palette record search: 'abdullah' among 100,005 users took about 820 ms and shows 5 matches, with no 'show all matches' entry.

Positive: English and Arabic RTL from the first screen (ar-AE locale gives dir=rtl, lang=ar on the sign-in screen). Alt+L switches in about 58 ms and survives a reload. The sign-out icon mirrors (scaleX(-1)) and breadcrumb chevrons point the right way. Table headers lay out right to left. Arabic plurals are correct (100,005 مستخدمين). Dialogs trap focus. Esc returns focus. Shortcuts match by physical key, so they work on an Arabic keyboard layout. The help sheet lists every shortcut. Contrast is at least 5.8:1 for muted text and breadcrumb links. No hard-coded UI strings were found.

Ratchet held: suite counts equal the committed minimums and the piece's ratchet diff only raises values. No earlier p04 verdict exists. The p00 r1/r2 gaps checked here stay fixed (no cross-tenant read through e-mail search or header switching).

human_gates.what: An Arabic-capable web font for screens and printed documents. Every maintained candidate (Noto Sans Arabic, IBM Plex Sans Arabic, Cairo, Tajawal, Vazirmatn) is SIL OFL-1.1, which is not on the allowlist. docs/decisions/p04-shell-fonts.md defers it to the owner, but gauntlet/needs-human.md does not list it yet.
